title: Transient edge pinning lifecycle guidance (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures operational guidance and an initial runbook for transient (TTL-based) region pinning at edge PoPs. Goal: provide a minimal, auditable approach that satisfies short-lived residency constraints (example: session-scoped locality or regulatory hold windows) without committing full data to a regional sovereign storage queue.

Background / motivation:
- Large enterprise customers are asking for fine-grained residency controls: not only long-term region pinning (customer-level), but short-lived locality guarantees for specific sessions or calls (e.g., health-data sessions, legal hold previews, short-term training hooks).
- Full region pinning is heavy (storage, SLA mapping). For many flows, customers accept a bounded TTL on edge-local handling that reduces latency and cost.
- This doc sketches how to support TTL-based pinning for inference KV caches, request-level artifacts, and ephemeral traces while preserving auditability and fallback safety.

Definitions (working):
- transient pin: an explicit instruction to hold a request or derived artifact in a target region/PoP for a fixed TTL (minutes->hours).
- pin-owner: the principal (token/customer-route) that requested the transient pin.
- enforcement boundary: the subsystem that guarantees pinned artifacts do not leave the region while TTL active (edge runtime + routing layer).
- leak: any artifact or runtime behavior that causes pinned data to be served or stored outside the pinned region.

Scope / what this doc covers:
- Edge-level caching and KV pin behavior for inference workloads (not long-term storage).
- Agent/ops procedures to inspect, revoke, or extend transient pins.
- Telemetry, audit evidence, and minimal legal attestation text.
- NOT covered: cross-region replication of customer S3; long-term archival pin workflows.

Key constraints and risk model:
- TTLs must be honored even under regional failure modes (best-effort extension vs forced eviction is a policy decision).
- We cannot rely on customer-controlled encryption alone: operator evidence must show routing and runtime kept data in-region.
- Cost: increased memory and GPU cache usage on pinned PoPs; we estimate 5-12% extra cost for hot-edge-heavy customers.

High-level design (concept):
1) Pin request API (controller):
   - idempotent call: POST /v1/pinning/transient with payload {customer_id, selector, region, ttl_minutes, reason}
   - controller assigns pin-id and writes a short-lived pin record to regional control-plane cache (signed, versioned).
2) Enforcement:
   - edge router consults local pin cache (fast path) to allow routing to local PoP. If no local pin, route per normal smart-routing policy.
   - pinned artifacts (inference KV entries, prefix caches, temporary traces) get a pin-id attribute and TTL enforced by local eviction.
3) Audit trail:
   - every pin request logs an immutable audit entry to a per-region append-only store (immutable logs are retained per retention policy).
   - audit entry includes pin-id, selector, ttl, customer-id, initiating-principal, and signed controller nonce.
4) Expiry behavior:
   - on TTL expiry, pinned artifacts are either (A) automatically evicted, or (B) optionally bulk exported to configured sovereign storage if customer requested longer hold. Default: eviction.

Operator runbook (quick ops cheatsheet):
- List active transient pins (CLI): rdi pin list --region eu-west1 --status active --format table
- Inspect pin details: rdi pin get --pin-id PIN-20240911-85
- Force-revoke (urgent legal take-down): rdi pin revoke --pin-id PIN-20240911-85 --reason "legal_take_down"
  - Expected response: 202 Accepted, revocation-job-id. Follow job with rdi job get.
- Extend TTL for a pin (only allowed if customer token permits): rdi pin extend --pin-id PIN-... --ttl +60m
- Export audit evidence for a pin: rdi pin evidence --pin-id PIN-... --format json --since 2024-09-01 > evidence.json

Sample audit line (human readable) to include with customer attestation:
- "2024-10-08T15:12:33Z | pin-id=PIN-20241008-11 | customer=acme-corp | region=eu-west1 | ttl=120m | action=created | principal=svc-account:acme-ingest | signature=SIG-..."

Failure modes and fallbacks (policy choices):
- Regional outage while TTL still active:
  Option A (default): failover disabled for pinned sessions -> return 503 to caller when PoP unreachable and pin required. This is the strongest residency guarantee but hurts availability.
  Option B: allow fallback to a nearby region with explicit recorded exception; creates compliance risk. Should only be allowed with explicit customer opt-in and recorded attestation.
- Stale pin cache on router -> router detects mismatch via signed pin nonces: if detected, route to control-plane to revalidate.
- Operator accidentally revoked pin: we keep a revocation audit trail and a 5-minute grace undelete window for mistakes for high-priority pins.

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor:
- Metrics to add: transient_pins_active{region}, transient_pin_create_latency_ms, transient_pin_evicted_before_ttl_total, transient_pin_revoked_by_operator_total, transient_pin_fallback_allowed_total.
- Dashboards: per-region pin heatmap, pinned-cache-memory-by-customer, pin-creation-error-trend.
- Alerts: pinned_eviction_rate > 1% for 30m, pin-create-failure-rate > 0.5% for 15m.

Legal / compliance attestation snippet (draft for security team):
"Redwood attests that while a transient pin is active, routing and runtime serve and store request-derived artifacts only within the pinned region/PoP. Audit evidence (signed controller records and per-region append-only logs) is available to demonstrate enforcement. Customer must specify TTL and whether automatic export after TTL is allowed."

Testing plan (staging -> canary -> prod):
- Unit: controller sign/verify of pin records; TTL machinery.
- Integration: end-to-end test using synthetic customer route: create pin, send inference requests tagged with pin-id, assert network path and cache affinity to target PoP.
- Chaos tests: simulate regional egress network split and confirm behavior per Option A and Option B variants.
- Compliance test harness: generate evidence bundle (audit entries + routing traces) and validate using internal attestation verifier.

Open questions / decisions needed (list):
- Q1: Default policy on regional outage while TTL active: availability-first (fallback) or residency-first (hard block)? (PD decision)
- Q2: Retention of per-region append-only logs and who can request them (legal, customer, regulator). Default retention 365 days? Need legal input.
- Q3: Support for multi-select pins (pin to several PoPs simultaneously) — cost vs usefulness.
- Q4: Is operator TTL-extension allowed without customer explicit consent? (scoped permission needed).
- Q5: Billing model for transient pins: should customers be charged for pinned-memory-hours? If yes, pricing model required.

Action items (next 90 days):
- [Owner: Maya] Draft API contract and minimal schema for pin requests (due 2024-09-25).
- [Owner: Ishaan] Prototype controller cache + signed pin token (POC by 2024-10-10).
- [Owner: Leah] Draft legal attestation wording and retention policy options (due 2024-10-20).
- [Owner: Samir] Implement a telemetry dashboard prototype for pinned cache utilization (trial data by 2024-11-01).

Estimated cost impact (back-of-envelope):
- Hot-edge memory + cache holds: +5-12% baseline infra cost for edge-heavy tenants.
- Audit-log storage: negligible at scale (append-only small records) but retention choices impact cost linearly.

Notes to reviewers (tone: brainstorming):
- This is intentionally conservative on enforcement — safer to start with residency-first defaults and allow opt-in relaxations.
- We should validate with 2 customers in pilot (healthcare and fintech) to surface legal constraints we missed.
- Keep CLI names intentionally short; UX follow-up needed with SDK owners.

End of doc (WIP).
